summary: Enterprise Suite AC-06 API DTO contract foundation for policy, group rollup, Workflow, incident, and ops metadata.

findings: The API crate is a thin DTO/conversion layer: serializable request shapes map into existing domain/app inputs and do not duplicate business rules.
Each conversion method is deterministic and side-effect free; validation remains in domain/app functions.
Stable camelCase JSON and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE enums give future gateway/runtime adapters a versionable contract seam.
The crate mirrors HR/payroll/accounting API DTO patterns while preserving no-runtime/no-storage boundaries.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: stable enum serialization and conversion into policy/workflow/incident/ops app paths would fail if DTO labels or field names drift
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests assert camelCase keys, stable enum JSON labels, error-envelope shape, and successful conversion into existing domain/app outcomes.
findings: AC-06 has direct contract tests for policy admission, group rollup, cross-product Workflow, incident rollback, ops command, and error envelope.
DTO names mirror existing domain/app intent, reducing translation burden for later HTTP/OpenAPI adapters.
One contracts.rs file demonstrates all preview endpoint request categories.
cargo fmt, locked API tests, locked API clippy, and 12-package enterprise regression tests/clippy passed locally.
Catalog rows and dependency-rationale allowlists were updated with the new API crate.

alternatives_named: skip suite API until HTTP server exists
put serde derives on domain structs
create a transport-neutral suite API DTO crate now
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A DTO crate provides integration-ready contracts without contaminating pure domain structs with serde or claiming runtime transport.
rejected_reasons: Waiting for HTTP would delay contract feedback and risk runtime-first API design.
Deriving serde on domain structs would violate the adapter boundary used by the other enterprise API crates.

findings: All request fields are metadata-only strings/enums/vectors; no credentials, tokens, payment instruments, or raw secret material are introduced.
Manual SSH remains a modeled enum path only so app/domain refusal can be tested later; no execution surface is added.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No deployed runtime path exists; conversion maps request vectors into domain vectors and performs no I/O.

findings.summary: DTO conversion cost is linear in supplied legal-entity/gate vectors and bounded by request payload size.

findings: Public request fields carry data_class annotations and catalog rows declare owned data classes.
The slice does not claim auth enforcement, DSR behavior, durable audit emission, statutory certification, or runtime API deployment.
The change is additive: one API crate, catalog rows, workspace membership, dependency allowlist, and spec/task pointers. It can be reverted without data migration or external resource teardown.
DTOs carry audit/evidence refs into domain/app inputs for future adapters, but no logs, metrics, traces, or audit rows are emitted by the crate.
Audit-chain JSONL rows capture local evidence and Oya VCS closeout only.
Enterprise Suite crate refs and contracts list now include the preview API DTO surface.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A suite API contract can be implemented ahead of HTTP only if it stays transport-neutral and delegates validation to domain/app code.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: existing HR/payroll/accounting API DTO crate patterns and specs/microservices/enterprise-suite.json developer_integrator target user
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Suite integration would lag behind child HR/payroll/accounting APIs and later HTTP work could invent incompatible shapes.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: OpenAPI/HTTP adapters should consume stable DTOs, not be the first place request shapes are designed.

findings: This slice makes Enterprise Suite composition externally contractable while preserving the existing domain/app foundation and non-runtime boundaries.
Names follow oya-enterprise-suite-api, existing DTO suffixes, and Enterprise Suite vocabulary.
Plan, todo, spec AC-06, crate refs, contracts, catalog, and dependency rationale all document the API DTO surface and non-claims.
API DTOs live in an api crate under the flat microservice path; domain and app crates remain responsible for validation and envelope projection.
No HTTP router/server, auth middleware, database adapter, Workflow client, OpenTofu runner, or cloud adapter was introduced.
Only workspace serde/serde_json already used by sibling API crates are added to the new API crate and dependency-rationales allowlists.
DTOs use serde camelCase request fields, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE enums, and a consistent ApiErrorEnvelope shape.
Conversion algorithms are explicit field mapping and vector mapping; no reflection or dynamic schema interpretation is used.
